Why {#Emph}hello{#Prev}, beautiful! And may my sweetest blessing be with you.
Wherever you may go, there's always {#Emph}drama {#Prev}waiting for you, isn't there?
May my blessings lift you like sweet nothings whispered in your ear.
I had the strongest urge to see you once again, and here you are, at last!
We're in this together, sweetness, and don't you forget it, {#Emph}hm?
Just remember, our war against ugliness is without end! Now let's fight on!
Anything that's worth doing is worth doing with passion! So come on, perk up!
Time again for another {#Emph}exciting {#Prev}night on the town! Lead the way, gorgeous!
We'll make them all go weak in the knees. And everywhere else, just in case.
So much beauty in this world, and if we don't fight to protect it, who shall?
I love what I do, especially when I get to take matters into my own hands.
Back to the comfort of the Underworld for the night? We'll pretty it up in no time!
You're headed {#Emph}our {#Prev}way again! My heart beats faster at the very thought!
Can this night possibly go even better than the last? Let's go find out!
Last night may not have been our best, but all that is about to turn around!
Doubtless this one knows hatred, not just love. {#Emph}In the name of Hades! Olympus, I accept this message!

2.Text: Why, {#Emph}hello{#Prev}, gorgeous! {#Emph}You {#Prev}look like you can break some hearts even {#Emph}without {#Prev}my aid! Oh, your brother would be so proud, knowing you're fighting for your kin!

1.Text: Passion strikes at the unlikeliest of times, spurring us past the limits that we know! Pray welcome it as I, and go with all my blessings, from the bottom of my heart!
You know, gorgeous, I like getting my way. And right now I would like for you to cut a bloody little path through every single wretch and traitor that dares get in yours. {#Emph}Please?
Oh no, you poor, poor thing, what happened on your way? There must be something I can do about your pitiable state!
{#Emph}Mm{#Prev}, you look as though you've had an altogether miserable night. Been there, gorgeous; I merely hide it well!
{#Emph}Ah{#Prev}, beautiful, you're {#Emph}hurt! {#Prev}How unforgivable. Whoever dared, I trust you ended their existence painfully!
You're {#Emph}wounded{#Prev}, love! If only I had reached you earlier. Though don't despair! Your heart yet beats, doesn't it?

{#Emph}Eugh{#Prev}, there's something very {#Emph}odd {#Prev}about this night, and {#Emph}certainly {#Prev}that ugly city of {#Emph}Ephyra {#Prev}doesn't help. But between my dear Hephaestus and Lord Ares and myself, I think you'll more than manage to get by.

{#Emph}Ohh{#Prev}, the Three Fates {#Emph}finally {#Prev}decided to make an appearance, just as we were getting used to not having them around. What grand prophecy do they have in store for us now, {#Emph}hm? {#Prev}Whatever it is, we'll handle it I'm sure!

If there really is another age that's coming up, then I say bring it on! True love never changes or goes out of style, no matter how much everything else does. Just stick with me and we'll be {#Emph}fine!

Gorgeous, you won the {#Emph}war {#Prev}for us! At least I think we won? Perhaps we didn't if these ugly Satyrs and the like are not about to leave yet, but you definitely did do {#Emph}something! Oh {#Prev}this is all too {#Emph}much!

That two-timing Chronos is on our side now? Against nasty versions of his older self, and invisible bits of Typhon we shouldn't fear {#Emph}too {#Prev}much but ought to heed. Not the strangest predicament I've been in, but it's {#Emph}close!

Some of the others wonder why you didn't opt to stay there in that big, beautiful House of yours in Tartarus, but they don't understand we need our freedom! Who moves back in with their parents after moving out?
I didn't think you'd keep heading this way once we were finished with Typhon, but you're not really finished with him, are you? Do give him my best for me if you see him, {#Emph}hm?
Hello, hello to you again, gorgeous! I just couldn't wait to see you any longer, so I thought I'd join you this time from the very start. You ready for me, {#Emph}hm?
My intuition told me you were just about to set off on another of your big important assignments, and I desired to be the first to see you off and give to you my very best!
The night is young, and we've a war to win, gorgeous! I thought I might accompany you from the moment you set forth. How about it?
Hold it right there, sweetness! You're not about to head into the dark of night without my aid, to help keep you {#Emph}warm and tingly{#Prev}, and our foes {#Emph}dead and buried!
Last time, you made a real difference here, you know! I shouldn't be surprised, and yet, a single goddess doing so much work? You're quite the inspiration, love! And {#Emph}terrifying{#Prev}, too!

It's been so long, love, why, I felt a little thrill of {#Emph}fright! {#Prev}But then a little birdie told me you'd gone far down in those depths, even to some success? I'll be excited to hear all the juicy bits!

You really got him, didn't you, gorgeous? A little birdie told me {#Emph}everything{#Prev}, how you fought all the way into those rancid depths, and took that Chronos {#Emph}down! {#Prev}Though, he's already back and angrier than ever, isn't he...?
Our emotions ran a {#Emph}little {#Prev}hot there, didn't they... I still can feel {#Emph}my {#Prev}heart racing, and if I'm not mistaken, {#Emph}yours {#Prev}might have been, too!
Oh, let's make up, what do you say, gorgeous? With everything that has been going on of late, I think we've all been a little bit on edge!
You know, I'm reminded one thing that unites us even in the worst of times is that we all have a {#Emph}bit {#Prev}of a temper around here!
It's no secret that I'm prone to fits of passion, and I'd not have it any other way. But you {#Emph}could {#Prev}have it differently next time!
Now I'll admit, that was a fight {#Emph}I {#Prev}started, love. Though, each time our passions run high, I think our relationship only grows richer for it!
{#Emph}Whew! {#Prev}Now, don't we feel better? We mustn't keep our feelings bottled up, even if it means having ourselves the occasional little outburst.
Now let's just simmer down and still the beating of our hearts! I am not angry anymore, though still a bit annoyed...
{#Emph}Hm{#Prev}, well, if there's ever a good reason to forgo my blessing, much less for the sake of my jealous kin, I've yet to hear of it!
Every relationship involves its little fights now and then. As long as we grow from them!
If you can't handle a bit of temper from me, then you don't deserve me anyway!
Getting rejected is never easy, especially as the most desirable goddess in the world!
Oh, you won my heart with how bravely you fought back there! All is forgiven. For now.
Aphrodite...

2.Text: She's back.

1.Text: Mm-{#Emph}hmm!

2.Text: My pleasure.

AphroditeRejection01.Text: Our world can be such an ugly place! Filled with such terrible misunderstandings as can veil the beauty we so often {#Emph}don't appreciate enough.

AphroditeRejection02.Text: Oh, gorgeous. If pride and vanity are truly weaknesses, then I'm about to let myself be very vulnerable with you here...

AphroditeRejection03.Text: I truly thought we ladies had a special connection, but then you do such things and make me feel unsure! And just a bit upset.

AphroditeRejection04.Text: I don't offer you my blessings so you can just save them for later like some sort of snack! You want something else, fine! You can {#Emph}have {#Prev}it.

AphroditeRejection05.Text: Try as I might, I just can't help but feel the sting of being spurned. And I don't like it, not a little bit. So now I have to sting you back!

AphroditeRejection06.Text: There may be those who can make peace with being brushed aside, but that's not something {#Emph}I {#Prev}can do, sweetness! No matter how hard I try.

AphroditeRejection07.Text: Oh, don't be such a {#Emph}tease {#Prev}with me! When I bestow my blessings, take them graciously next time. But now...?

AphroditeRejection08.Text: Sometimes I think we shouldn't force you to play favorites, but we shouldn't do a lot of things, I'm sure! Such as get angry with {#Emph}you!

1.Text: You'd side with dear Hephaestus over {#Emph}me? {#Prev}There must be some mistake, sweetness! Which means there too must be some sort of {#Emph}punishment...
You {#Emph}could {#Prev}stay out of these infrequent little spats I have with my hard-working Hephaestus. But if you {#Emph}really {#Prev}want to get involved, why, {#Emph}sure!

AphroditeRejection11.Text: I'm really not accustomed to rejection, and shall {#Emph}not {#Prev}get used to it because of {#Emph}you!

1.Text: Age before beauty, is that it? For I can think of no other explanation for what you've done!
Hello, sunshine!

2.Text: Hello, Cousin!

1.Text: Perhaps you knew this Boon was going to be mine, for how can my light be contained, even in a heavy parcel? It must have been glowing a {#Emph}little {#Prev}at least, right?
Normally my light makes it easy to spot whoever needs a blessing or a smiting, but you always seem to be in shadow! Fortunately, Charon seems to know how to get a hold of you!
It's fortunate the Underworld Boatman's still plying his trade even during a downturn such as this! I trust his prices have gotten better, at least? Or, perhaps worse...
We have to reach you however we can, and Charon's been more than keen to oblige. Bit of an odd fellow, but then, aren't we all?
That Boatman's something of a coin collector, isn't he? Well, once we're finished with old Chronos, all those Gold Crowns of his will be extremely rare collector's items!
We started working with Charon back when we had to figure out a system to transport all the mortal dead down to your father's realm. Must be more pleasant hauling messages from us!
Mess with me, and it's lights out, sunshine.

2.Text: Need I remind you, I'm not always as nice as I look.

3.Text: Best not push the bounds of our relationship too far.

4.Text: I'm no less prone to wrath than any of us, Cousin.

5.Text: We Olympians can't all be the best; because it's my job.

6.Text: You left me little choice but the old show of force.

1.Text: I, {#Emph}erm{#Prev}, lost my train of thought, Cousin, for Aphrodite here, she doesn't seem to understand the meaning of a {#Emph}private conversation. {#Prev}Lady, would you care to join us, then?

2.Text: Oh, dear Apollo, {#Emph}yes{#Prev}, I {#Emph}always {#Prev}care to join your conversations, {#Emph}especially {#Prev}the private ones! And is there any who could blame me? Love and sunshine go together, after all!

1.Text: Ares and I were just chatting about how we seem to get on best when we're on the same side of a war. So, Brother, is this all an elaborate ploy to bring us closer together?

2.Text: I think it's merely that a proper war brings out the best in all of us; even in you, Apollo, and in me. The rigors of conflict forge unbreakable bonds! And make for powerful blessings.

1.Text: All of us here want you to succeed, Cousin, though none so much as Lady Demeter... I'm reminded that you are her grandchild, after all. {#Emph}Erm{#Prev}, wait, she wants to speak to you herself!

2.Text: Thank you for your advocacy services, Apollo. Should I have need of them again, I shall apprise you. For now, my granddaughter requires our abilities, not honeyed words.

1.Text: You know, Cousin, one thing you and Hephaestus have in common is you don't seem to get a lot of sun! I often try to coax him from his cave, and while I usually fail, not {#Emph}this {#Prev}time!

2.Text: Come off it, mate, before the witchie catches on to your routine! Now make yourself useful over here, lest I stick this hammer right where {#Emph}you {#Prev}don't get a lot of sun!

1.Text: I know you were expecting me, sunshine, but my {#Emph}glorious {#Prev}stepmother the Queen would like a word! This instant... so I'd better step aside, all right?

2.Text: You see, my dear? There are yet those upon Olympus who show their Queen the proper deference. Seek not to earn the love of your subjects; make them a bit afraid, instead.

1.Text: Great Hestia has joined us here, Cousin! Returned from all her journeys 'cross the world, to lend her wisdom in our time of need. Where glows her hearth-flame, you shall also find my light. And together, we can, {#Emph}oh—!

2.Text: {#Emph}Oh {#Prev}shut it, Golden Boy, we don't have time for pageantry! Instead, how about we show your wee cousin there how we can light up the night? Won't do for her to wander in the dark!

1.Text: Cousin, our uncle and I were just debating what to do about mortals who turned their backs on us... I think a year or so of plague should settle up the score! But, Lord Poseidon here thinks it's more important to {#Emph}go big...

2.Text: Why would you {#Emph}not {#Prev}go big, given the choice, my delicate nephew? I'll shake the earth so strongly it shall swallow all those nasty mortals up, and deliver them straight down into the arms of your comely cousin there!

1.Text: {#Emph}Erm{#Prev}, greetings, honored Cousin! I'm here now with none other than the bringer of thunder and lightning, magnanimous King of Olympus, your great Lord Uncle and my illustrious father, Zeus!

2.Text: Oh, {#Emph}haha{#Prev}, my niece and I are well past such a level of formality, my son! Though while we have the pleasure of her company, what say we show her how we put the {#Emph}light {#Prev}into {#Emph}lightning?

1.Text: It's him...
We'll shine so bright it hurts!

2.Text: No hiding from {#Emph}this {#Prev}light!

1.Text: Oh {#Emph}now {#Prev}you want my aid?

2.Text: Well I don't see why not!

1.Text: Hey little brother!

2.Text: Apollo?!

1.Text: Far too much blasted light...

2.Text: The light of the {#Emph}sun?!

1.Text: It's Apollo...!

2.Text: Hi Apollo...!

1.Text: Thank you for this, Cousin!
Cousin Apollo! I am grateful for all your warmth, benevolence, and aid! Please, accept this gift!

2.Text: An offering, for me? What a delightful surprise, and I haven't had a lot of those of late. Know what, I've something for you, too!

1.Text: I wonder, does this bottle's brilliant sheen come from the god of light, himself? Perhaps to him it should return, right now!

2.Text: Such a thoughtful gift! It's gracious of you to think of me like this, and during such a time. Though there's no need to go out of your way!

1.Text: Brilliant Apollo, your many talents must be the envy of all the land, and I am honored that you're sharing them with me. Here, this is for you!

2.Text: Come now, you truly shouldn't have. Such flattery's entirely unnecessary, I assure you! Although it's perfectly welcome!

1.Text: They say this Nectar shines as brightly as the sun, Cousin. May it live up to such a promise, especially now that it's yours! I'm beyond fortunate to have you as a friend.

2.Text: Oh, you're too kind. You didn't have to get me {#Emph}this! {#Prev}I never knew you Underworld gods were so damn courteous. You know our customs better than {#Emph}we {#Prev}do!

1.Text: My glorious cousin! It was you who first reached out to me of all those on Olympus. I've come this far because of you, and no matter what happens, I'll never forget the kindness you showed me.

2.Text: Come on, the pleasure is mine! It's not all sunshine on Olympus recently. But then I hear from you, and I'm left feeling everything will be all right. Don't quite know how that happened, but I'm very grateful that we met.

1.Text: Dear Cousin, you must have Nectar in no short supply. But I know that the depth of the sentiment is what distinguishes one bottle from the next. So please accept this one; it should be good.

2.Text: I'm an Olympian; I'm used to glad-handers and sycophants. Everybody wants our favor, right? And I can smile and nod better than anyone, even Father. Yet with you... well, if only we had more chances to talk than trade in courtesies...

1.Text: Lord Apollo, my cousin, my friend! This Ambrosia reminds me of the moment I first saw your father's palace and heard your wondrous song. Thank you for letting me see our world in a new light, and for always believing in me.

2.Text: Believing in you couldn't have been easier, Lady Melinoë, even without this Ambrosia dancing with moon beams from the Crossroads. I feel truly blessed to have met you, and that my sister found you when she did. You're the greatest boon our family has received in a long, long time.

1.Text: Word of advice about good Lady Aphrodite? Don't get distracted. She speaks of love and beauty, though she's no stranger to conflict. Perhaps my power can offset her own.
Between us, I have never seen Ares so pleased as he has been recently. And I can probably imagine why. This war that we've been waging... it's a real piece of work, even for him.
At least my good half-brother Ares finally made an appearance. I was beginning to wonder if he'd ever show up! Though, he might have wondered that about me in the past...
If Artemis was terse or impolite with you, don't take it personally, please. It's how she is with everyone. Always been the solitary sort, and we never know where she is when we need her.
My half-sister Athena knew your brother well, and sends her regards. She's preoccupied with our defense, leading our front-line forces and all that! She regrets that she can't aid you thus.
Couldn't help but notice there's no {#Emph}bow {#Prev}in your arsenal! Artemis and I, we figure why sully our hands when we can settle any ugly business from afar... although your magick may suffice!
That Chronos is up to something, but not even Athena knows what. His assaults on Olympus always fail, even if they've kept us occupied. What's his next move...?
To think we'd wage war against our own grandfather. Not that we should give Chronos that sort of credit. He's a disgrace to our line; a hateful Titan, not a god. Not family.
I rather hoped old Chronos and his ilk would have seen the light by now, but alas. We'll just have to keep shining it in their faces for a while.
You've struck a solid blow against the Titan's forces, but they've started to regroup. Still, these types of victories must shake them to the core. Let's drive them back!

They're saying you got Chronos, didn't you, sunshine? Last night at least, but that's the deathless Titans for you! Never staying down for long. Though you've something in mind for that, my sister says...
So you were born and raised in some secluded grove down there? No luxuries, mortal worshipers... so much living to catch up on once this ugly matter is resolved.
When Artemis first told me about you, I couldn't help but think of Demeter. She couldn't be there for your mother when Chronos struck, but I know she'll do everything she can for you.

You can count on most of us, but I can't speak for Dionysus; don't even know where he is! I like a feast as much as anybody at the proper time, but the god of wine thinks the proper time is {#Emph}all {#Prev}the time.
Still no sign of Dionysus. I'd be worried if it wasn't him, but he gets like this. Sometimes I {#Emph}cannot {#Prev}believe we're related. I want a bit of order around here, he wants the opposite.
You must be in the city of Ephyra to the west, a staging ground for our enemies... with the Underworld gates thrown open, Chronos can replenish his forces faster than we can kill them off.
Wonder what there is to do for leisure down in Erebus, when one isn't rigorously training to vanquish hateful Titans and such. There must be something...

We've confirmed sightings of that {#Emph}Eris {#Prev}buzzing about. She's from your realm not ours, so you may be more privy to how come she's showed up uninvited! Though, that tends to be her style. Somebody needs to shoo her away, already...
I don't like getting swept up in our family's petty feuds, especially with older generations that apparently have nothing better to do. But you and I couldn't exactly sit this one out, could we?
No wonder Chronos hates us, right? Admittedly we've got some prickly personalities here, but for all our quirks, we're family; and we stick together. Something Titans wouldn't understand.

I didn't think matters could get much more precarious for us, but if the Fates are truly gone, then... their prophecies about the future may not come to pass. They foretold our family's eternal rule over the world... what if they were wrong?

Even if you managed to make Chronos see the light, the Three Fates are still missing. And we're supposed to believe he doesn't know where they are? This couldn't possibly be what they wanted or foretold...
You're in the Mourning Fields. I wonder does the Hyacinth grow there... the flower of a gentle prince, long gone. Once the Underworld reopens, perhaps I could go seek him out.
Well, sunshine, it's just the two of us again, now that you slaughtered every... what exactly do you call those? Well, no matter, here!
I never was particularly close with your father, but I guess neither were you. Always struck me as a gloomy sort, though he did seem to care a lot about his own. He'll get his justice yet.
Our world's been through worse times than {#Emph}this, {#Prev}Cousin! So I am told at least, I've not seen anything this bad. Still, it's nothing we can't handle, right?

You trained under Hecate, the Witch of the Crossroads? She's well respected here, though we've not seen her in a while, of course. I often speak ill of Titans lately but I'm reminded that they're not all bad.

It's complicated who owns what up here. You know Helios the Sun? He's back to tramping across the sky in his chariot like nothing's changed, but he'd be lost without {#Emph}my {#Prev}light! {#Emph}Eugh{#Prev}, Titans. What can you do?
Hephaestus has been hard at work on our defenses, so I'm pleased you've heard from him. Don't take his surly manner the wrong way! He doesn't get out much, certainly not these days.

{#Emph}Ah{#Prev}, you've met my stepmother, have you? I'm fortunate to feel loved, but Hera, well, I'm not her favorite. Long as no one leads her to believe you're Zeus's child, you will be just fine.
You got there faster than expected, which might mean you got a bit of a boost from Hermes! He's swift for sure, though I can never get a straight answer out of him about anything...
Sometimes I think Hermes must still be running about in the Underworld like he used to, as lately I can't seem to find him anywhere. He's been so cagey with me, too! Some messenger.
Hey you got old Hestia to crawl out of the woodwork! She normally wants nothing to do with any of us, though this business with Chronos got her all worked up. Well, good!
It's often said there's nothing new under the sun, though I've not seen a weapon quite like what you're wielding there! The legendary Arms of Night, Hephaestus says. Impressive stuff!

I always wished to see the House of Hades, though your father and mother have a royal guard I {#Emph}may {#Prev}have sent to their realm prematurely. It'd make things rather awkward if we ran into each other there...
See, sunshine? Whenever you head out with the Harmonic Photon that you got from me, I won't be far behind. And you'll get a warm fuzzy feeling for good measure!
That Photon I gave you has seen plenty of good use by now, hasn't it? I know you don't always need a light in the darkness like so many others, so I'm pleased it could help.
What sort of light can I provide for you today? I've got hard light, soft light, blinding light, last thing a mortal ever sees light... you name it!
You ever wonder what light really is, Cousin? Can't grasp it in your hand, doesn't weigh a thing, yet it's all around us! A real mystery... I'm waiting for the mortals to figure it out!
You're more of a night person, aren't you, sunshine? Accustomed to the dark. Me, I'm more the broad daylight type, but hey, to each their own.
Don't know how you managed all this time without so much as a ray of light down there. Different worlds, I guess, but sometimes good things happen when such worlds collide.

When Artemis first told me your tale, I figured it was just one of her pranks. Taking on the Titan yourself, {#Emph}come on. {#Prev}But it {#Emph}did {#Prev}sound like something a vengeful child of Hades might attempt...
What is that fancy staff you've got, with a serpent coiled at the top? How strange, it's... reminiscent of a vision that I've had... about a masterwork that can do no harm...

Mortals look to us for guidance and inspiration. They must be {#Emph}horrified {#Prev}by what they're seeing of late! Half of them seem to be against us now. Let's hope it's the {#Emph}other {#Prev}half that's left once all this is over.

For such a fearful lot, mortals sure love killing each other! There was this war they had a while back that even had us gods at one another's throats. I tried to settle it with plague and arrows and such, but {#Emph}no! {#Prev}Father wanted it to play out.

Lately I'm reminded just how frail mortals are... I never let myself get attached anymore. They can be so much like us, even beautiful, but there's all heartbreak watching them die. Their deaths aren't even the end, but they sure act like it!
Artemis says you're rather musically inclined! Runs in the family, even your parents have an ear for it what with Orpheus as their court musician. He's the best I ever taught!
Where in blazes are you now, sunshine? It's like you're at the bottom of the sea. Wherever it is, it's awful dark, and as you know, I've always got the cure for that.
We'll keep holding it together on this mountaintop, just as long as you keep holding it together... wherever it is you happen to be! Take care, all right?
Wait, you're right on Olympus now, sunshine! So close to us, though I am painfully aware the worst is yet to come as you press on. Fortunately, I have the best for you right here!
I can't believe we've let those Satyrs overrun our mountainside... leave it to Dionysus to try and make friends with them, but I've had no such fortune, believe me.

Don't know what it is exactly but something about this night made me flash back to when first you contacted me in those very woods. Well, either strange forces are at work or just my imagination, right?

You're just outside of the Ephyra gates, aren't you? That city is beyond salvation; I know they used to worship your mother and father there, but still... if it were up to me alone, I'd sweep the place away and start anew.
There's something exceedingly odd about tonight. Haven't we already had an evening just like this, down to the smallest detail? Your magick at work perhaps... as long as it isn't Chronos.
Wait how exactly did you even get there, sunshine? Last I checked you were traversing someplace else entirely! But then I had a hunch to check {#Emph}again{#Prev}, and sure enough...

I know you're not one to complain, but it couldn't have been easy for you being at the Palace here at the break of Dawn... probably much more light than you're used to. We're hardly used to it either now thanks to all of Typhon's storms.
I like being the god of many things. There's light, and poetry, music, healing... so many passions, and all the time in the world. Why settle for just blacksmithing or what-have-you?
The sightless Cyclops Polyphemus bars your passage, does he now? Don't know what good my light will do against the likes of {#Emph}him{#Prev}, though perhaps I can help get you there in one piece.
Beneath our uncle Poseidon's affable veneer is a ferocity I've learned to carefully avoid. If he's backed you with his ocean-strength, you're better off. Go make the most of it!

Prometheus himself, leading the assault against us... one of our sole allies amongst Titankind, become a bitter foe. All because of how we treated him! Or because... he knows which side shall be victorious when all is said and done...

Didn't think we'd let Prometheus continue his assault like this. Some partnership we've formed, all so you can re-create the path you took to Typhon, to then face the monster's remnants on the summit as before...?

If Prometheus truly had the foresight that everything would happen as it did... why bar your path and fight so fiercely, only to be defeated again and again...? Unless the dawning of a new age wouldn't come about in any other way...
Bit embarrassed to admit that I'm the god of prophecy, among everything else. I ought to have seen this Titan business coming! But I didn't... and old Chronos caught us out.
As god of prophecies, I'm certain that we're going to succeed. Exactly how, though, I can't say for sure. That's prophecies for you! Blasted frustrating things most of the time.

When I first reached out to you many nights ago, I figured, {#Emph}hey, another cousin! I like those! {#Prev}But the truth is I never expected you to make as great a difference as you have. My hope is I've done my part to make it possible.

Aphrodite's been quite excited for you... she has a way of knowing everybody's supposedly-private lives, but if she's blessing your relationships, you're better off. Some of mine certainly could have used it...

So you get to pick your poison between going after Chronos in the Underworld, or coming to our rescue here! Truth is there's been some dispute as to which is the brighter idea. But, you must know what you're doing better than we.
You seem fairer than ever, Cousin. Awash in moonlight...  you're working with Selene, aren't you? And here I thought she'd be too busy galloping across the sky to back us up...
The light of day {#Emph}can {#Prev}be a bit harsh, so it's fortunate the Moon offers such a pleasant alternative. Selene's shine may be more to your liking, if you can even see her from there...
Such a dark and oppressive night this is shaping up to be... even if I could illuminate all your foes waiting in ambush, I'm not sure you'd want to see them. Be very careful out there...

My sister Artemis once also trained with Hecate, you know! Trained in {#Emph}what{#Prev}, however, I have no idea. I still remember how they'd howl at night like a pack of wolves, {#Emph}heh{#Prev}. Bit unnerving, honestly!
My word, you reached the {#Emph}surface{#Prev}, didn't you, sunshine? I thought your birthright meant you couldn't live up here...?
The surface used to be more pleasant. But ever since the siege, Uncle Poseidon has been going all out with quakes and cataclysms in response. Stirring up the land like it's his mixing bowl.
Cousin, weren't you headed to Olympus last I checked? Must have been waylaid by the Titan's thugs. Well, don't give up! Although I guess you wouldn't be there if you did.

{#Emph}Erm{#Prev}, we've got a situation starting to unfold. A big crevasse opened up at the base of the mountain, and something's in there... something big. And it's {#Emph}breathing... {#Prev}suppose it's friendly...?
I caught merely a glimpse, though that was poetry in motion the way you handled yourself against that lot. Talent runs in the family! Some of us just wound up with a bigger share.
How fares your voyage here, sunshine? If only we could whisk you over with more-godlike means, but the skies are as treacherous as the waters... as I suspect you've noticed.
Do bide your time, sunshine. The Titan thinks he has us pinned, but we have the situation here under control! Just locked in a bit of a stalemate is all.
{#Emph}Augh{#Prev}, this blasted war. Leaves little time for music or for poetry or any of life's joys. Though, it's brought the family closer together, I guess!
You were a little easier to spot with twin torches in hand... though yours don't seem to cast the customary kind of light! Truly the more I learn of you, the more questions I have!

Ever wondered just how gargantuan is Typhon, the Father of All Monsters, truly? Well, you need but pay a visit here and you'll find out! Till then, {#Emph}erm{#Prev}, we'll... just have to fend him off!

Judging by all his vengeful roars, Typhon must hate my father almost as much as Chronos does. But are they truly working together? A monster such as that couldn't possibly be taking orders from a Titan, or anybody.
Chronos must have thought nothing could stop him if he unleashed Typhon, but he thought wrong. Let's throw everything we've got at him and finish this, sunshine.

So we're now working to prevent even the {#Emph}possibility {#Prev}that Typhon could have overwhelmed us here? And the Titan's forces are somehow part of this new plan. Well, if you're in, {#Emph}I'm {#Prev}in. Should make my evenings more exciting for a bit!

I still can't entirely believe you {#Emph}got {#Prev}him, sunshine! Typhon should have taken the combined might of our entire family, and in a way he did, it's just... the rest of us were busy fighting back his swarms. He's really got us stretched thin.

If Typhon keeps coming back, eventually there may be no mountain here left to climb. I know my father and Queen Hera have a plan in case things could not get more dire, but I'm more optimistic for whichever plan you have in mind...

We should be able to hold back Typhon for a while longer, especially now that you've shown us a thing or two about how it's {#Emph}done{#Prev}, sunshine. You're going after Chronos now, aren't you? Well ridding us of {#Emph}him {#Prev}certainly wouldn't hurt.

Even though your mother and father are back, you can't just stroll down to the bottom of the Underworld, can you? Finding remnants of Chronos means re-creating the conditions in which you faced him before, something like that...?
So you're a witch, are you? Interesting craft. Your magick-making words possess a certain rhythm and power. Poetry is much the same! Except its magick affects only the heart.

So pleased you finally got to meet your brother by the way! Me, I have {#Emph}more {#Prev}than enough of those, but if you grew up as an only child, you could probably use one. And it's never too late to make up for lost time.

My father Zeus already got to you, did he? {#Emph}Blessed {#Prev}you, I should say! He's a god of many inclinations. But when our rule is threatened, or even insulted, no one fights back more fiercely.
Let's show them a dazzling display they won't soon forget.
Won't take but a moment here and you'll be positively radiant, you'll see.
I'd rather we handled all this in the light of day, but whatever works!
Brighter days are ahead, just have to get through this rough patch.
What can we do but try and make these dark days a bit brighter, Cousin?
You're going to put on a brilliant performance tonight, Cousin.
Peace will come again eventually, but for now, we have a reputation to uphold.
From all of us upon Olympus, we are grateful for your ongoing support.
Must be something I can do to brighten up your evening there a bit?
Go on, sunshine, and may my light help guide you where you need to be.
Can't have a nice day out in the sun, well here's the next best thing!
You're brilliant without my light, though here's a little just in case.
Much as I'd rather offer poetry and music, right now these shall have to do.
Where there's light, there's hope, sunshine, so get set for some of each!
Oh, this is going to be a sensational night, I can already tell!
Your foes won't so much as touch you once we dazzle them a bit.
I'd cast a plague upon our enemies but think you'll do the trick.
Tread lightly down there, and remember, we're with you all the way.
Remember, don't go heading down into the dark without a light.
I confess I'm rather enjoying this particular song and dance.
My light normally can't reach the depths of the Underworld, but you can change all that!
We're all in this together till the end, sunshine! Whenever {#Emph}that {#Prev}is going to be, right?
I don't like getting swept up in family affairs, but I couldn't exactly sit {#Emph}this {#Prev}one out.
As god of prophecies, I'm certain that we're going to succeed.
Talent runs in the family! Some of us just wound up with a bigger share.
Look at you, strutting through that Underworld as though you own the place!
Don't know how you managed all this time without so much as a ray of light down there.
What sort of light can I provide for you today?
Don't know about you, but I've got a good feeling about how this is going to go!
You were a little easier to spot with twin torches in hand!
Such a dark and oppressive night this is shaping up to be...
Before you go charging off to battle and glory once more, please, allow me!
May this blessing be of benefit every step of the way tonight.
For all the Boons we've offered, you've given us quite the blessing in exchange.
I like being the god of many things... so many passions, and all the time in the world!
Just a spell, it's just another spell. Ten words... {#Emph}In the name of Hades! Olympus, I accept this message!

2.Text: Greetings from Olympus and well met, there, sunshine! Look, we can't get to the Titan, but if you truly mean to stop him, then the least I can do is light your way down.

1.Text: All right, sunshine... what do you say we cut the song and dance and set you up with something positively brilliant this time. See here!
There's no one god of vengeance on Olympus, because we all share that responsibility at times. Go on, take back what's yours.
You seem a bit out of sorts, sunshine. I'm supposed to be the god of healing, though even I can't aid you all that much in your present state. But let me see what I can do.
{#Emph}Eugh{#Prev}, you seem unwell, Cousin. Either you're pushing yourself too hard, or your foes landed a few too many hits. Perhaps both. Take care, all right?
I'm a bit of a physician, sunshine, and my professional opinion is your vital signs are not the best right now. Although perhaps we can still get you back in shape...
{#Emph}Eugh{#Prev}, looks like I've run a little late, as you most likely could have used assistance from me prior to whatever gave you such a thorough drubbing. Try to hold on, all right?

The Fates are back, all three of them, sunshine! Such a relief to feel their prophecies again. They even now foretell the dawning of a new and different age. Plenty of time to prepare... though let's make the most of it, right?
How did there come to be so much deceit in this world, Cousin? Believe me, we've needed a god of truth around here sometimes. Happy to do it and hope it catches on.
Hope you don't mind I call you sunshine, by the way! I mean it when I say it. I know you come from underneath the earth, but there's this brilliance about you. Your mother's side I guess.
There anybody special in your life? A princess like yourself must have suitors of all sorts. I've had my share, though I'm not the marrying type, and besides, I don't think Hera would oblige...
For all the Boons we've offered, you've given us quite the blessing in exchange. Olympus has powerful allies... well, you and Heracles, at least! But you have this spark so many others don't.

It was a joy and honor to accompany you to the Crossroads on Selene's silver chariot, Cousin. The ballad Artemis and I performed... that's the first we jointly composed. We don't always get along but you inspired us.

I'm impressed our fathers reached an agreement about Chronos, and {#Emph}certainly {#Prev}did not expect they'd send him to the Isles of the Blessed! Best spot in all the Underworld, so I hear. May he keep it that way!

The song Artemis and I composed, we call it {#Emph}Time Belongs to Us. {#Prev}Came up with it when our hope of overcoming Chronos was starting to slip, but my knack for prophecy told me we had to hold on...
Just getting started for the evening, are you, sunshine? Don't know about you, but I've got a good feeling about how this is going to go!
The night is young, and I found you already. You don't suppose some of my sister's tracking skill is starting to rub off on me, do you?
Before you go charging off to battle and glory once more, please, allow me! And may this blessing be of benefit every step of the way tonight.
Thought you could use this extra bit of preparation before heading out again in earnest, Cousin! A bit of extra reassurance that you'll make it all the way.
Look at you, strutting through that Underworld as though you own the place! Although perhaps you do? Not sure how it works with the succession plans down there.
The other evening, we lost contact with you in the deepest level of the Underworld. Soon after, though, our enemies flew into disarray, at least for a while. Your doing wasn't it? Fine work!

You found a harmful trace of Chronos, now a trace of Typhon's next? Glad there's no real sign of them from where {#Emph}we {#Prev}sit... besides their scattered forces and the devastation that they caused, but that can be cleared up!
Oh, enough of this. Let's turn our combined might back in the same direction, and move on.
That got a bit ugly, didn't it? How about we both stay focused on the task at hand.
Forgive my little outburst there, would you? Just a bit of bad temper. Runs in the family.
A momentary flash of anger was all! We gods are easily hurt, for a bunch of immortals.
You were just messing with me back there, right? I normally can take a prank just fine, but we've all been a bit on edge.
No use keeping anger bottled up. We're gods! We control everything but our emotions, right?
Relationships grow stronger through adversity. So ours must have grown a little stronger there!
{#Emph}Erm{#Prev}, sorry about that, sunshine. When my wrath flares up, probably best to not be anywhere in the vicinity.
Well, so much for that lot! May my blessing serve you better than them. You earned it!
I let frustrations get the best of me, but that entertaining spectacle shook me out of it!
That light...

2.Text: He's here...

1.Text: Naturally!

2.Text: For certain!

ApolloRejection01.Text: You wound me, Cousin. After everything we've been through together, you'd brush me off so easily?

ApolloRejection02.Text: {#Emph}Augh! {#Prev}Now really isn't the time for petty squabbles, but I'm afraid you leave me with no choice...

ApolloRejection03.Text: Not your first choice?! Perhaps you haven't heard, so I'll enlighten you: My generosity is not unlimited.

ApolloRejection04.Text: I have few weak points, but my pride is one. You got me where it hurts, so now I've got to get you back.

ApolloRejection05.Text: Was it something I said or did? Or perhaps you don't respect my power. Even when it's turned against you thus?

ApolloRejection06.Text: I go out of my way to offer you my strength, and you refuse? That's not something any self-respecting god can abide.

ApolloRejection07.Text: Come on, sunshine, why the snub? You should know that when my feelings get hurt, it's never the only thing.

ApolloRejection08.Text: I have a reputation to live up to. I can't just let you brush me off like some pathetic commoner with nothing but a prayer!

ApolloRejection09.Text: Perhaps someday we'll all be able to resolve our differences more sensibly. But we're the gods, and we're a family, damn it!

ApolloRejection10.Text: Beneath this sunny disposition, I have something of a vengeful streak, Cousin. Though I know actions speak louder than words.

1.Text: I greet you.

2.Text: {#Emph}Ah{#Prev}, yes.

1.Text: {#Emph}Ah! {#Prev}It seems this message was successfully delivered in utter secrecy! We ought to take more such precautions, although perhaps it would hinder your ability to plan.
You need not be surprised to find me thus. Our family often takes a more-direct approach, but I am not above skulking in shadows; I rather quite enjoy it.
In war, one must prepare for {#Emph}all {#Prev}eventualities. This could have been one of your other kin lending their Boon, but I was swift to take decisive action in their stead.
Our blessings are difficult to resist, are they not? Even without knowing which you shall receive, let alone whose, you are always willing to pay the Boatman's price.
The river-boatman may no longer ferry souls into the Underworld, but has become quite valuable to the ongoing war effort. He's quite effective with that oar of his!
There were occasions on which I would pay the boatman's fare myself, so many souls did I send down at once into the Underworld! Those were good times.
War cannot endure should supply lines be disrupted for too long; so I am ever-grateful for your Boatman, as I'd not have reached you now if not for him.
Gold is a fascinating metal, is it not? Mortals often fought and killed over the stuff. Only the rarest Gemstones from your father's domain appeal to them more!
Either you are with me or against, my kin; no in-between.

2.Text: You must have thought this little war would go {#Emph}your {#Prev}way.

3.Text: I am unmerciful by nature, if I didn't make it clear?

1.Text: Love and hate, my kin! The most powerful emotions, and the underlying causes of war. So it is that glorious Aphrodite here has taken interest in my leanings, and I in hers.

2.Text: Your preoccupations are my passions, Lord Ares! What would drive someone to lose themselves entirely to feeling? I would like to know {#Emph}every {#Prev}last possible reason.

1.Text: I was just speaking with fair Aphrodite here about how much she's learned of war during the many conflicts we have overcome. Few would admit that there is beauty in the act.

2.Text: Oh, definitely {#Emph}yes{#Prev}, my lord! The gleaming weaponry and chariots, the ranks of men prepared to die, and just the glory of it all! Besides, there can't be beauty without ugliness!

1.Text: My half-brother Lord Apollo here claims he was first amongst our family to reach you thus, my kin. Perhaps if {#Emph}I {#Prev}had in his stead, this all could have been well over by now...

2.Text: Oh come on, Ares, you've never been big on bringing conflicts to an end. Probably why you showed up so late to this one! But you saw how great a time the rest of us were having and just {#Emph}had {#Prev}to get involved.

1.Text: I am impressed with how our great goddess of seasons here has taken to our war. The more personal we make it, the more bitterly we fight! Is that not so, dear Lady Demeter?

2.Text: It was not I who made this personal, Ares. Perhaps if at some future point you have your own children and grandchildren taken from you, then you shall understand. For now, however... you need but to comply.

1.Text: Hard-working Hephaestus and I are the only true-born sons of the King and Queen of Mount Olympus. I keep telling him, we ought to rise to the occasion, and assert ourselves!

2.Text: Want more responsibility, Ares, have at it! Otherwise I don't know what you're after, and don't want any of it, Aphrodite notwithstanding. Got my forge, got my wife... it's enough.

1.Text: I wish never to burden my mother the Queen, so heavy is her crown; but she insists on being here, perhaps believing that my aid alone shall not suffice. Is that quite so, Mother?

2.Text: Spare me your concern, Ares, and whilst in company, address me not as {#Emph}Mother. {#Prev}If I cannot trust you with basic matters of decorum, whyever should I trust the efficacy of your {#Emph}blessings?

1.Text: I'm pleased to see dear Lady Hestia putting her capabilities to greater use. Why, here she is right now! I always knew you had a disposition toward destruction, Goddess, as so prevalent is flame in war!

2.Text: It's a side of myself I don't often like to show, as much as you seem to like seeing it, Ares. I figure we can't properly control our powers if we can't control ourselves.

1.Text: Our Uncle Poseidon here tends to give counsel more than any of our kin, perhaps believing volume of advice is tied to quality. What ought to be our current course, Uncle?

2.Text: Our current course ought to be straight toward our foes, where we can smash them like a tempest does a ship! {#Emph}Ah{#Prev}, but I feel all fired up and fit for battle! Come to think of it I always get this way when my good nephew Ares is around!

1.Text: Forgive me here, my kin, but my Lord Father and I, we were in the midst of a discussion that I felt ought not to wait... concerning what I learned whilst visiting more-distant lands.

2.Text: Oh calm yourself on that account, Ares! We had best deal with matters close to home prior to worrying about that which may be amiss in distant corners of the world! We'll deal with {#Emph}them {#Prev}in time.

1.Text: The warrior sigil...
All shall suffer!

2.Text: Let there be {#Emph}war!

1.Text: How utterly {#Emph}depraved!

2.Text: Have you no {#Emph}decorum?

1.Text: Was that {#Emph}Ares?!

2.Text: {#Emph}Ares{#Prev}, is that {#Emph}you?!

1.Text: The vicious god of war...

2.Text: I'll show that Ares real war...

1.Text: Ares, it's {#Emph}me!

2.Text: {#Emph}Come on{#Prev}, Ares...!

1.Text: This I accept from you, my lord.
Lord Ares, I know mortal warriors often would make offerings to you before their battles to the death. I likewise wish to pay you my respects. No mercy for our foes!

2.Text: I shall not take such honors without giving in return, especially from one who understands my work. A living weapon such as you ought to have {#Emph}this.

1.Text: It's not for me to decide how many battles I have left; but knowing I have your support in them means a great deal, my lord. May we achieve all our objectives soon enough.

2.Text: Such Nectar often is withheld till victory. Although in many ways, I feel as though we have already won! I have, at least; and to that end, I'll find a moment to enjoy this properly.

1.Text: No war can last forever, but we shall always be family, isn't that so, my lord? This is but a simple reminder that there's more to unite us than the thrill of the fight.

2.Text: You've given me far greater gifts than even this fine Nectar, which I do of course appreciate. But the slaughter you have thus far caused... that is truly second-to-none.

1.Text: I find that there are moments when the thrill of battle practically consumes me; a feeling I once tried to suppress. But now I realize it leads to victory... and {#Emph}you{#Prev}, my lord.

2.Text: I used to think no others in our family shared preoccupations such as mine. In this I'm pleased to have been very much mistaken. Whenever the whim to dole out death strikes you, know I shall be there.

1.Text: I did not know what to expect from you before we met, Lord Ares... but I've found that you have a certain candor others lack. Thank you for always being clear with me.

2.Text: I must admit, I do not frequently receive such offerings because of my demeanor. Many are so {#Emph}easily {#Prev}unsettled, by honesty, by various passions; you seem not to be, my kin.

1.Text: I wonder, Lord Ares, when mortals on opposing sides all pray to you for victory, how do you choose whom to bless? I trust this offering has no such complications.

2.Text: Such gifts are welcome to a point. Mortals believe they can gain favor from me, but it is their own will to fight that most determines how quickly they die. I appreciate your interest in these smaller details!

1.Text: To all our triumphs in the past or still to come, Lord Ares! But this Ambrosia is not merely for that... I know you also learn from painful losses and defeats. In this especially, I find we are alike.

2.Text: I share the sentiment, my hellborn kin. Our family tends to focus overmuch on victories; we do not look unflinchingly at failures and defeats, where deeper insight may be found. In this and more, you have been a welcome exception.

1.Text: You know, I wouldn't offer you my blessings readily if not for fairest Aphrodite, who I see has graced you once again. You've seen the beauty in my work, and it is thanks to her.
My half-brother Apollo graced you, has he now? Whilst I pursued my one vocation, he chased flights of fancy, growing talented at many different things, yet having mastered arguably none.

The goddess of the hunt is by her nature seldom to be seen; I've often tried persuading Artemis to use her talents on the battlefield, not merely in the woods. But she is stubborn, as perhaps you know.

My dear sister Athena has a great burden to bear, beyond that heavy suit of armor that you've seen. Not only does she manage our defenses, she must answer for the failures thereof. I trust her wisdom shall help see her through.
If our grandfather seeks war, then who am I to deny him such a thing? Neither is the irony of such a matter lost on me; I simply think we {#Emph}all {#Prev}can get what we desire.
The goddess Demeter is known for causing crops to flourish... though, she may as easily spread famine 'cross the land. Such power is the ideal complement to mine.
Our bickering over whose favor you decide on first? Pageantry, destructive and uncalled for! A war we wage within to settle our disputes. It's something of a tradition!
{#Emph}Oh{#Prev}, how the city of Ephyra reeks of death! I practically can breathe the stench from here. Now only wretchedness and misery remain, all of it well beyond salvation I should think.

I understand the goddess Eris hounds you quite incessantly each night that you approach. I have to say it puts me in a bit of a predicament, for Strife has benefited what I do far more than most. Yet I know that she cannot be controlled.

The goddess Eris is quite unpopular up here, and I expect also where you reside. But I have certain sympathies for her, shunned as she is. We cannot change our nature; we deathless gods, we cannot even be destroyed, it seems.
There is some kinship 'twixt you and the incarnate of Strife? I thought perhaps a bitter feud and nothing more. Yet you apparently see Eris as I do. We are all forces of nature, are we not?

Though I may be the firstborn son to our King and Queen, I have no greater share of influence. We all offer our counsel, but who's heeded, who can say? I'm oft reminded that, in war, diplomacy can play a vital part.
I understand that the Three Fates are held against their will? I would be more concerned for them, except... perhaps this means that war itself shall finally be the sole determiner of its results...!
I owe your father a great deal, for the more work I did, the more he'd have to do in turn. I trust that he valued our collaboration for his part? It hasn't been the same without him since.

My poor brother Hephaestus, relegated to a life of toil in a foundry... creating arms and armor that have seen such glory as he'll never see himself. At least he's been of use to {#Emph}you{#Prev}, my kin.

My dear mother the Queen is careful not to show any member of the family undue favor, not even the children to whom she gave birth... I like to think that my propensity to be objective comes from her.
My mother Queen Hera sees war as altogether distasteful, and often tries to distance herself from it. But not this latest one! I scarce recall when last we were together for so long.
You've met my mother's champion called Heracles, famed amongst mortals for his rugged skill. His club has claimed perhaps more lives than you! Though he had a head start.
A successfully conducted war requires crisp communication, for which we still depend on swift-footed Hermes. It is to be expected that he reached you first; with blessings not mere tidings, I trust.
You have inspired the reluctant Hestia to join this fight! To think her flame serves mostly to warm mortals' homes. I {#Emph}so {#Prev}wish to see her use it to its fullest potential!

That Sword Hilt which you bear belonged once to a warrior who spilled much other blood before his own. It is of common fashion otherwise, but worked so many battles that I feel a connection; perhaps you do as well.

By now that Sword Hilt which I offered you has seen such bloodshed in your care that I should think its former owner would be pleased! At least {#Emph}I {#Prev}am most certainly, both to contribute {#Emph}and {#Prev}observe.
The witch Medea is of service to you, yes? The plagues and poisons for which she is infamous in some respects reduce the possibility of war; but they achieve results, so one must keep an open mind.

I sense that you possess an artifact from Doom himself! I have crossed paths on more than one occasion with Lord Moros, for my area of expertise often requires his. This must be an exciting time for him!

Before the Titan took the Underworld, a daughter of the goddess Nyx would often punish those who took more than their share. She was called Nemesis, and I admired her... perhaps of late she's seeking retribution for her kin.
Now that is an exquisite weapon you possess! The Rock Lion Mace has a storied, bloody past, and you shall grow its legacy. I never knew it was a form of the Nocturnal Arms...
I knew the goddess Nyx, my kin, and learned from her about your realm and its customs. She and your nearest relatives were very close. If now it takes a war to win them back, so much the better.

The goddess Nyx, returned unto the Underworld, my kin! Although I felt quite melancholy at the thought of our war drawing to a close, I am most pleased that the presence of Night Incarnate is more strongly felt again, as well it should.
The markings on your armaments are reminiscent of the goddess Nyx. I know she oversaw the forging of the Nocturnal Arms, but she once wielded them herself...?
Of late, my obligations have required me to go abroad, for I can only do so much from our quite-isolated mountaintop. But now there's so much to take care of here at home!
There is a stir of something different in the air tonight... you feel it too, yes? The sense of great and ancient possibility. Let us bring it into being through sheer force.
I admit even we gods may be subject to forces beyond our knowledge or control. I sense such influences even now... intensifying this great war of ours. Spurring us to act.
I regret not having had the opportunity to give you my regards whilst you were here, my kin. But the need to dispose of trespassers took precedence. I trust we may yet meet in time?
Our uncle Poseidon puts on a veneer of confidence, yet I believe that it is perspiration, not sea-water, often visible upon his brow. War can be disconcerting, certainly.

Clearly Prometheus the Titan is no stranger to conducting war. He knows, for instance, just how fragile most alliances can be. Do you suppose he stood with our fathers in the past only to better learn their weaknesses?

I always took Prometheus for a mere pacifist, so readily did he accept his fate when he was caught defying my lord father's will. Since found his fighting spirit, has he? At times it takes some pain and suffering to discover who we are.
You and Prometheus are to perpetuate your conflict, then? He has his complicated reasons why, which my kin have accepted grudgingly. I am simply pleased to see him fight.
What forces could have brought you suddenly as far as you have come? Perhaps there are such Underworld gods whom even we cannot detect; allegiances of which we need not know.

Pain and death contain so many mysteries, my kin. Each Satyr, each Harpy whose life you take, their sacrifice has something to teach us. And you have learned voraciously; may our studies continue far into the future.

You've slain at least a thousand Satyrs thus far during your campaign; a modest army, single-handedly destroyed! And that is but a {#Emph}fraction {#Prev}of the sheer totality of the destruction you have caused!
Upon nights such as this, what sole illumination can be found is from Selene on her shining chariot aloft. You have her light about you, my kin; her hidden power as well, yes?

Such terror permeates the atmosphere this night. It almost feels as though the goddess Nyx herself has touched the hearts of all those who oppose us, such is their fervor. This battle shall be difficult I think!
Do you detect a certain fear that hangs in the air this night, my kin? I suspect yes; perhaps you are its very source... a goddess not merely of the Underworld, but of nightmares themselves.
I recognize that ornate scythe you bear; it ought be in the hands of Death himself! Though in yours, close enough. To think that even Thanatos was taken by the Titan unawares.
A growing number of terrific wars are lately being fought at sea, my kin. You are in some respects leading the charge on the evolving nature of the craft!

I recently returned from certain travels, for my work is never done. I was pleased to see that matters here were well in hand; much better off than when I left, in many ways. I take it you're to thank in no small part?

Colossal Typhon is an even greater threat than I could have imagined, my kin! How envious I felt, hearing the tales of our elders fending off the Father of All Monsters... but now, we all are witness to his wild rage firsthand!

The Father of All Monsters, slain! I scarce believed it when I heard, but my lord father and dear mother quite insisted this was true. It seems that you possess a power {#Emph}far {#Prev}more terrifying {#Emph}even {#Prev}than our vanquished foe.

I'd certainly not call our latest battle against Typhon anything close to a victory, yet we were able to repel him finally after your forced retreat. But now it seems he has resumed his slow ascent...
It has been long since I witnessed the goings-on beneath the earth, not that mere Boons allow me to see much. Some of those dark places you lay waste to, I scarcely see at all.
When shall your father restore passage through the Underworld's gates? Perhaps his realm is not in the condition yet to take in so many new residents at once. Well then, all in good time.

I have to say I was reluctant to participate in these affairs at first. A war must run its course; I often set the wheels in motion, yes, but then observe impartially. This one, however, has become a bit of an exception.

War can be such a complex thing. I can bring it into being, yes, but soon it takes on a life of its own; perhaps akin to rearing a child! And this child with whom we're dealing now has grown a bit unruly, I have to say.
This is by no means the first occasion that our family has become embroiled in a war. Yet I have never before seen a case that swept so many of us up! I get a bit emotional about it still...

I know the weapons which you wield; glorious Nyx told me of them herself! I've an insatiable hunger for such knowledge, not unlike how the Nocturnal Arms cannot be sated whilst your realm remains under duress.
Knowing my brother Hephaestus, he could identify each one of your dark armaments by name! But I recognize their purpose and their form, and wish to see how much destruction they can cause.

You're reminiscent of your brother quite a bit. A consummate dealer of death he was, born in the pressures of the deepest hells! Although perhaps you wouldn't get along, just as my siblings and I have our little spats.

You're reminiscent of your brother quite a bit. A consummate dealer of death he was, born in the pressures of the deepest hells! Although perhaps you wouldn't get along, just as my siblings and I have our little spats.
Your brother Zagreus is doing well? I trust that you shall get on famously, for you have much in common: brutality, mercilessness...! Would that I had such a sibling here...

Lord Father Zeus is most experienced at war, having both fought and conquered many times. Yet he often favors counsel from Athena over my own, even as she struggles to defend this mountain. At least you see we should {#Emph}attack.
My father's blessing is most-powerful indeed. The strength to vanquish Typhon himself! Although this circumstance in which we find ourselves has still-greater demands, and I stand ready to provide.
The thunderous might of Lord Zeus is already yours; what need have you of my comparatively pitiable strength? Although perhaps such differences are not as great as once they were...
Nothing compares to witnessing the slaughter of one's enemies, don't you agree?
Wherever blood is to be shed, I can be counted on at least to be intrigued, if not involved.
Mortals all must die; I merely wish for them to do so in a fitting way.
There are such conflicts as can only be resolved with violence; no need to fight the urge.
Wherever there's a wave of death, I seek it out, and lately, there you are.
Life spreads much like a plague across this world, but there are ways to keep it to a manageable flow.
No single war may last forever, yet no single war shall ever be the last.
How readily your enemies commit themselves to slaughter, time after bloody time.
Pain and suffering tend to subside, so this shall be a reminder for all involved.
Bloodshed can often be avoided, yet I seek never to let such opportunities slip by.
Such times in which we live, when even the dead can still experience the full extent of war.
Let us savor these moments whilst the ashes of destruction come to rest.
The spirits of the dead haunt every battlefield, do they not? Perhaps you can even see them there.
War is in our very nature, thus not something to reject, but to embrace.
Violence does not always put an end to conflict, but can reduce it to a simmer for a while.
Your each and every battle is a pleasure to behold, my hellborn kin.
So many wars are lost to time, but this one perhaps shall not be soon forgotten.
A war that spreads across the surface, and below... we have outdone ourselves, my kin.
Let's not perpetuate this bloodshed for vengeance alone; there are many perfectly good reasons.
Some find my work to be unpleasant! You have witnessed it firsthand, and know the truth.
So many battles to be fought! It can be almost overwhelming, that I know.
Victory in war is bittersweet; but the end of anything is rarely the best part.
There may appear to be no perfect outcomes in my work, although perhaps you'll come to see it as do I.
Whilst I admire your efficiency, do take a moment to appreciate the calm after the storm.
Each night gives us fresh opportunity to enact slaughter in entirely new ways.
For the greatest conflicts, I am always willing to provide my services, and bring about a sensible result.
We all have a will to fight, is that not so? I merely seek that we be truer to ourselves.
Your battle for this eve has just begun, and I wish not to miss a single kill.
If there is to be bloodshed this night, then let us make every drop count.
How are we to assert our dominion over this world, if not through violence?
Violence is not always strictly necessary, but it often works.
Whoever said that violence never solves anything likely never even tried!
May you slay all who oppose you with as much efficiency or cruelty as you like.
The Earth drinks deeply of the blood you spill, and I would see you slake her thirst.
So many foes within your father's realm lack flesh and blood, but they shall have to do.
To think that war could rage even beneath the earth; what an exciting time!
You mean to carve another bloody path up to our mountaintop? Then that I wish to see!
The remnants of the Titan's legions have a battle-hunger I feel warrants some respect.
War isn't for the squeamish and the weak, but you've a real taste for it, I see.
I so look forward to seeing which methods you employ against your enemies each night!
Perhaps we need some sort of rally-cry tonight, my kin. Would {#Emph}kill them all {#Prev}suffice?
Was beginning to think this one would never show his face. {#Emph}In the name of Hades! Olympus, I accept this message!

2.Text: {#Emph}Ah{#Prev}, a fellow student of death! To have confronted monstrous Typhon with such zeal. My kin insisted that I act upon the violence spiraling out of control, and I do wish to see your prowess, so {#Emph}here... {#Prev}a first of many contributions to the cause.

1.Text: I'm quite partial to such wars as have a certain ebb and flow... when the upper hand is hard earned, and easily ceded! For now, my kin, it's yours. Hold on to it.
In war, the victor is whomever is the strongest or the most ruthless of all. Although I too have a degree of influence, and bestow on you that very power {#Emph}now.
Your blood runs red just as your brother's did, and you've lost quite a bit already for the night. I only wish I could have reached you sooner, to have witnessed more of it myself.
Such grievous wounds you suffer from, my kin! In war, of course, no one gets out unscathed. May you inflict {#Emph}far {#Prev}greater suffering on any who would dare to do us harm.

So much life already lost this eve; although I should not use that term myself. Lives extinguished are never {#Emph}lost{#Prev}, always {#Emph}spent... {#Prev}if but for the good of your father's realm.
You suffer injuries which would have caused even the strongest mortal to succumb; but you fight on as though you are unscathed! Perhaps you even find a thrill in it?

The Fates have been discovered after all? And they intend to take a break from all their traditional manipulations? I do not entirely believe it, but... war would be so exhilarating were its victors never preordained.
It is quite common to experience mixed emotions at the outcome of a war! And to have been denied a violent resolution to our plight... although from what I gather, there is violence still to come.
This latest war shall not be easily surpassed; admittedly in part because we gods were at the center of it. But I trust another shall exceed it at some point! One always does.

We're to continue warring with the Titan Chronos but in different {#Emph}times? {#Prev}Or different circumstances, I should say... had you but failed to succeed before. A fight without an end... {#Emph}oh{#Prev}, my kin.
How many of these Chronos impostors are we dealing with, do you suppose? To think we shall eradicate them all, one at a time. Yet no two battles are to be the same!
I understand you are somehow still able to confront the Father of All Monsters here! So then his raging spirit yet remains, in some dark recesses of time. Would that I could look upon him there!
As you set forth on this night's campaign, I would accompany you from the outset, so that you may fight and slay your enemies entirely without restraint.
I sensed the possibility of concentrated violence from your current whereabouts. Soon then, the killing shall commence. You need but choose the means by which it shall be done.
Your latest effort to stop Typhon did not go as you presumably desired, yet we still were able to use the diversion you created to our advantage. Now for the Titan Chronos, yes?
How soft the earth you walk upon must be, and not from rainwater, I think. Well if you wish to tour war-torn landscapes near and far, then let me be your guide.
You've quite a distance to traverse until you reach the battlefield that is our mountainside; though rest assured, fighting shall be fierce along the way!
To have driven back the Father of All Monsters is a monumental achievement, my kin. But the war is not yet won! Which means still-greater victories await; perhaps with the occasional ignoble defeat.

Such a monstrosity, Typhon... slow, enormous, stubborn as he clambers toward our highest peak; driven by vengeance, rage...! In some respects I do admire him. Though I am grateful you were there to dash his hopes.

Word reached us that you defeated the Titan of Time last night, and we were most impressed; but I was left to wonder whether he experienced the throes of agony before the end. Perhaps he eventually can be dissuaded thus.
I was not even born when first our fathers slew the Titan Chronos... and neither could I see him thwarted by your hand last night. But I've a good imagination for such things.
I thought that I might find you there tonight. Whilst the Titan Chronos reels from your recent victory, his forces on the surface must be shaken, and more vulnerable to attack.
In war, we must be unpredictable. The Titan Chronos likely is expecting you to strike at him again, whilst you direct your efforts toward our mountain here. A clever ploy.
An exquisite performance befitting our lineage! You are to be rewarded for all that.
Sometimes I like to benefit the losing side, to give them a false hope.
Do you suppose your foolish enemies believed they had you there?
An occasional show of hostility is just how we assert ourselves, my kin.
So many battles to be fought, yet I just cannot help myself sometimes...
{#Emph}Ah{#Prev}, but that was excellent, although the best this eve perhaps is yet to come.
You've satisfied my need for retribution, or at least my thirst for blood. For now.
I sense that no survivors of that clash remain, save you. A fine outcome.
To the victor of the battle, a reward. And I, in turn, experienced quite the spectacle.
My work at times requires me to side against my kin. You understand, of course?
This was but an inconsequential skirmish, and even still, it was such a delight.
Your foes believed they stood a chance; such optimism fascinates me to no end.
The god of war...

2.Text: Here for the violence...

1.Text: Certainly.

2.Text: Of course.

AresRejection01.Text: You realize what this means, don't you, my kin? I trust I do not even have to say the words.

AresRejection02.Text: Bitter wars are sometimes waged for less; really over nothing much at all.

AresRejection03.Text: Perhaps this was a mere misunderstanding, though I tend to presume malicious intent.

AresRejection04.Text: My other kin also at times brush me aside, and look where {#Emph}that {#Prev}got them.

AresRejection05.Text: If you truly wish to war with me, you'll find I'm more than happy to oblige.

AresRejection06.Text: I truly feel for you my kin; no recourse but to choose a side, and suffer the result.

AresRejection07.Text: It would be a lie to say it brings me little pleasure to do what I now have to do, my kin.

AresRejection08.Text: I do not begrudge your decision; I am most-grateful for it, since it means I can do {#Emph}this.

1.Text: My dear brother has been chosen over me before, and neither did I appreciate it then.
I would have chosen similarly in your stead, but have my pride nevertheless.
You're wise to side with Aphrodite, though for now you've made an enemy of {#Emph}me.
A calculating choice, perhaps. But not without its violent repercussions.
After such a simple Trial, surely you would attempt another?

2.Text: I have observed all that I wish for now.

3.Text: This facet of reality is clearer to me now.

4.Text: Thus you have proven that this possibility exists.

5.Text: All this was a mere possibility before.

6.Text: I am grateful, though that shall be all for now.

7.Text: This particular experiment was a success.

8.Text: A mere thought, turned into a real possibility.

9.Text: The bounds of what is possible continue to expand.

10.Text: This was a chance I trust was well worth taking.

11.Text: I was sufficiently amused by your attempt.

12.Text: This Trial is complete; I bid you return whence you came.

13.Text: I have observed the outcome of this Trial with keen interest.

14.Text: You may go no further; that is all part of the Trial.

15.Text: I am satisfied with the results of this Trial, and bid you return.

16.Text: You have accomplished what this Trial asked of you.

17.Text: I did not necessarily expect that you would pass this Trial.

18.Text: Another Trial successfully completed, Spawn of Hades.

19.Text: You passed; but now return to shadow, Spawn of Hades.

20.Text: May my Star Dust compensate you for your services.

1.Text: Although you failed this attempt, I was amused.

2.Text: I understand reality can be quite difficult to bear.

4.Text: This outcome was but one of many possibilities.

5.Text: I did not observe as much as I would have liked.

6.Text: An inconclusive result in our experiment.

7.Text: Expected outcomes can be disappointing nonetheless.

8.Text: I do believe the possibility exists that you succeed.

9.Text: This type of failure was a highly probable result.

10.Text: Small variances in your actions led to this.

1.Text: It seems my mark has had an undesirable effect.

2.Text: This is all part of our experiment.

3.Text: I take it this was not the outcome you desired.

4.Text: Thus my mark is washed away, for now.

5.Text: Life is ever-capable of folly, is it not?

1.Text: Whatever this is... it's remarkable, truly.
If you'll permit me, Almighty Chaos, I wish you to have this gift of Nectar, in accordance with my family's custom among relatives and friends. None of this would have been possible if not for you...

2.Text: Then I shall grant you this wish, and the freedom to bestow upon me further gifts as you see fit. For I have familiarity with this custom of yours, and am prepared to reciprocate.

1.Text: Almighty Chaos, I wish to exercise my freedom here by giving you this. Though I suppose you probably could have made it yourself...

2.Text: This Nectar that you offer me is quite an interesting substance. When I created the fabric of reality, I had a sense of the ways in which it could be used; but I did not necessarily anticipate all possible results, including this one.

1.Text: I know such sweetness as this Nectar is never to be taken for granted, Almighty Chaos. Please, it's yours! Wondrous creations such as this are only possible because of you.

2.Text: Such gestures are unnecessary to the arrangement between us. If this is an act of supplication, then simply speak your mind. Although I sense no deeper motive presently...

1.Text: You can sense my motive in giving you this. Sometimes we simply feel an impulse to express our admiration. Knowing how important your whims are to you, surely you understand.

2.Text: The Olympians often demand tribute from their worshipers, do they not? Their custom, perhaps, but not mine. I merely ask that you honor our arrangement in perpetuity. Though neither shall I reject your offering.

1.Text: It's heartening to know that the Origin of All Existence also is a source of such limitless curiosity. Here's to finding great interest even in the simplest of things!

2.Text: Substances such as this Nectar... is it not interesting how they can be made, but not unmade? Everything, in essence, is itself. Thus your offering to me is truly unique in its own right. And I thank you for it.

1.Text: Such a strange journey your creations take, Almighty Chaos! This particular bottle, for instance... formed after untold aeons, only to find its way back to {#Emph}you. {#Prev}Inevitably or not.

2.Text: I still possess some of the Nectar that your brother once gave to me, when he was dealing with a certain quandary of his. I think that I shall keep this offering close by to that. You follow in his path, yet seem to choose your own way.

1.Text: Almighty Chaos, please accept the greatest delicacy for which my family is known. I know it's less than nothing in a way; but for us, it's a symbol of the bonds we share.

2.Text: I am unmoved by this Ambrosia that you offer me yet understand this substance is considered valuable and relatively rare. I wonder why you give it to me now, and wish to know; therefore, respond.

3.Text: You seem to like unguarded truth, Almighty Chaos, and it's that I am very much in awe of you. Your attention and your aid mean more than I can say. My family gives Ambrosia when mere words cannot suffice.

4.Text: Your insufficient words have been of greater impact than your gift; I shall accept it all nevertheless. You are amusing, Spawn of Hades, more than I originally thought.

1.Text: {#Emph}Erm... {#Prev}cheers?

Does there remain a place for beauty and for objects of desire in a world such as this? The goddess Aphrodite must think so, and you work now as allies. I believe it a worthwhile cause; this world was born of a certain desire, after all.
The golden son of Zeus has given you his blessing, I see. Apollo was not always so willing to involve himself in your family's struggles. Perhaps the present matter gives him little choice.
You bear the Boon of violent Ares, who often worships me more than his kin; for without creation, there can be no destruction, he says. And I believe he is entirely correct.
